findings: 20+ photos recommended (we used 10-15 — may explain drift)
75 word prompt max — overloading dilutes Soul tag
Lead with Soul identity FIRST, then style cues
Specify lighting explicitly (softbox, rim light, golden hour)
Avoid sunglasses, masks, extreme expressions in training photos
Training takes ~5 minutes
Structure prompts like a director: number shots, action per shot, escalation arc
Multi-shot in single generation — character stays consistent across shots
Input up to 9 images + 3 video clips (15s each) + 3 audio clips (15s each)
Audio generated alongside video — lip-sync + ambient + music in single pass
2-second hook framework: open with strongest visual beat
Camera encyclopedia: name specific camera moves in prompt
Prompt Bible exists (escape9to5.ai/armory/prompting-guides/higgsfield-seedance-guide)
GitHub skill set: 15 Claude prompt skills for cinematic, 3D CGI, anime, e-commerce
Product URL import is fastest path — backend dedupes by URL
Transparent PNG backgrounds = more scene flexibility
One primary preset per product line per quarter for brand consistency
3 pacing variants from same preset: short hooks, standard posts, paid cutdowns
Concise prompts: materials + light + motion (not creative writing)
Brooklyn skincare startup: +12% CTR over template-based ads from 2 product images → 7 reels
Node-based infinite board connecting prompts → generations → refinements
ALL models available as nodes (Soul 2.0, Seedance, Kling, Nano Banana, GPT Image 2)
Soul ID characters persist as reusable nodes across campaigns
Outputs from one model route into another — pipeline orchestration
Team editing with version history
Pay only for model runs — graph building is free

Specify light intent (soft morning, controlled studio, rim highlight)
Describe camera path (slow arc, steady push-in, macro focus shift)
Leave room to breathe — negative space signals confidence
Motion should feel guided by intent: smooth, measured, never frantic
Slow dolly-in, soft studio key light — plain language works
SoulID = visual identity anchor: lighting, tone, motion settings stored
